summary: Steel tower first operated on Wickaboxet Rock in 1926, decommissioned in 1973 and moved to a Cranston correctional institution; current status unclear.

facts.status_note: The list marks it gone. The 2008 register text says it was a guard tower at the institution; no source confirms it stands there now.

access.note: Last recorded use was as a guard tower at a correctional institution. No source describes public access.

events.note: Register says first operated in 1926 on Wickaboxet Rock; it gives no separate construction date.
Moved to Cranston after decommissioning; the register gives no separate move date.
Registered as Wickaboxet Rock Tower Site, US 61, RI 8.

evidence.supports: 65-foot steel tower, first operated 1926, decommissioned 1973, moved to the Cranston institution and used as a guard tower
evidence.quote: This 65' steel tower was first operated in 1926. It was decommisioned in 1973 and moved to the Adult Correction Institution (ACT) in Cranston and is used as a guard tower there.

evidence.supports: Site entered the register on September 8, 2008
Original site is in Kent County
Cranston ACI entry is listed as gone
Wickaboxet Hill entry is listed as gone

corrections.why: The register says the tower was moved to the Cranston institution and used there as a guard tower. Whether it still stands there is not confirmed, so check before changing.

sources.title: Wickaboxet Rock Tower Site, Former Fire Lookout Sites

notes_for_editor: Status unresolved. The 2008 FFLOS text says the tower was in use as a guard tower at the Cranston institution, but the FFLA list marks both the Cranston entry and the Wickaboxet Hill entry gone, and no source dates any removal. The register spells the institution Adult Correction Institution (ACT); the story uses that name without the acronym, which looks like a typo for ACI. The official name was not checked against a state source. The story no longer says the tower should not be visited: no source supports that, so an editor may add a safety note if wanted. A Facebook post seen only as a search snippet (not readable here) gives 1934 for the tower's erection, against the register's 1926 first operation; unverified and not used. The register's 65 ft is not said to be measured to the cab floor. The 'private' access level is my reading of 'guard tower there', not a source statement about visits. No photos found.
